title: Seeing the Invisible: How Vision-Language Models Read, Predict and Trace Radio Fields
author: Yiyang Zhu, Xin Li, Guangyuan Liu, Ziheng Liu et al.
description: Operating in the physical world requires reasoning beyond what cameras directly capture. In a city, radio signals are invisible to the lens, yet their strength is governed by the buildings and streets an image does show. Given only these visible structures, can vision-language models (VLMs) infer the invisible radio…
summary: Operating in the physical world requires reasoning beyond what cameras directly capture. In a city, radio signals are invisible to the lens, yet their strength is governed by the buildings and streets an image does show.
takeaways: This yields RadioVISTA, a benchmark and training dataset for visual reasoning about invisible fields.
Open models fail even earlier at reading the field itself, and are systematically wrong, scoring below random guessing even when credited for any of four attempts.
On unseen cities, fine-tuning brings a 9B open model close to frontier proprietary models on fields, yet neither supervised nor reinforcement fine-tuning improves path tracing.
